obligations.definition: Tag hit requires the captured read-request valid, a matching captured tag for the stored request address and the current validity bit of its captured set. In both-way hits the binary way is one. A miss selects way0 for data. Each set independently replaces way0 after reset and thereafter replaces the opposite of its most recently touched way. A lookup hit touches its hit way; a refill touches its pre-edge replacement way. A hit and refill in one set give the lookup touch priority; different sets both update. A refill sets only the selected way valid and has priority over global invalidation. When no refill occurs, invalid_i clears all way validity bits but preserves SRAM contents, replacement state, MSHR, FIFO and pipeline. An invalidation coinciding with a refill is discarded, with no pending invalidate.

obligations.definition: A stage1 miss offers block address addr[31:3] for one edge. Each of four entries is live when either of its two subentries is valid; a matching live address is secondary. Match encoders bitwise-OR all matching entry indices, returning0 on no match. Allocation uses the lowest free entry or subentry, returning0 when none exists. Reject a primary when all entries are live, a secondary when its two slots are full, or any miss concurrent with a response for the same block. Rejected misses are dropped without core backpressure/retry. An admitted primary writes its block address at the pre-edge lowest free entry. Normally it sets that entry's subentry0; concurrent response for a different block clears the matched response entry and places this new valid bit at the smaller of the free-entry and response-entry indices, while the block write remains at the original free entry. Thus reuse can revive the old response address. An admitted secondary sets its chosen slot, with new valid bits taking priority over concurrent clearing. Without an admitted request, a response clears all subentries of its selected entry.
obligations.setup: Fill all4 entries with memory requests blocked, issue secondary misses up to/over2 slots, and issue a fifth primary. Cross response/miss same block rejection, different block reuse on either index ordering and secondary slot clear/write priority. Predict block/valid state from input history and check later visible memory requests/refill placement.

obligations.definition: mem_rsp_ready_o is always one. A two-slot FIFO captures every valid memory response and consumes each nonempty head at the following rising edge; it has no empty bypass, may simultaneously enqueue/dequeue and preserves stale slot payload while empty. Its99-bit payload is {data64,address32,source3}; response source is otherwise ignored. The head address bits31:3 match all live MSHR blocks and bitwise-OR matching entry indices; no match selects entry0. Every consumed head refills the stored block address of that selected entry, not the raw external response address, using its current replacement way, stored block tag/set and the head's full64-bit data. Unsolicited or duplicate responses therefore use entry0's stale block and clear its MSHR validity. Response acceptance/consumption is independent of core valid, flush, invalid and memory request readiness. Complete native high bits and all documented concurrent reset/read/write/admission priorities remain in scope.
obligations.setup: Inject isolated, consecutive, duplicate and unmatched responses with complete high-bit data patterns, source variations and mixed request traffic. Track the two physical FIFO slots and pre-edge head. Compare one-edge refill latency, selected entry's stored address fallback, concurrent request/response reuse and source independence. Require nonempty independent checking and directed plus randomized histories for each criterion.
